title: What is known about 1RB1RC_1LC1LE_1RA1RD_0RF0RE_1LA0LB_---1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RC_1LC1LE_1RA1RD_0RF0RE_1LA0LB_---1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to an Antihydra-like map. Lean's kernel proves that the machine halts from blank tape iff the orbit of an explicit map (n ↦ 3n/2 + 2, counter +2, for even n; n ↦ (3n+7)/2, counter −1, for odd n) drives the counter below zero, and that the first 10,000 rounds do not. In 105 rounds the counter never goes below 1; a random-walk model gives a chance of about 10−11 that it ever does.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 62,542 cells have been visited and 44,391 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.052).

claims.title: Every round, in closed form
claims.text: For all n, m: from R n m = A> 0 11 (01)^n 0 11 (01)^m the machine reaches R (3n/2+2) (m+2) for even n, R ((3n+7)/2) (m−1) for odd n and m ≥ 1, Z ((3n+9)/2) for odd n and m = 0; from Z k = A> 0 11 (01)^k it reaches R ((3k+1)/2) 1 for odd k and halts for even k. Built from 8 symbolic rules and an induction on the sweeps.

claims.title: Halting reduced to the map
claims.text: The machine halts from blank tape iff the orbit of next from Z 1 (reached in 10 steps) reaches Z k with k even.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 rounds
claims.text: The map, evaluated by the kernel; n then has about 5,800 bits.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>5</sup> rounds
claims.text: The counter is never below 1 (lowest at rounds 1 and 4) and is 50,008 after 10<sup>5</sup> rounds (49,997 odd rounds, 50,003 even). The first round starts of a direct simulation agree with the map.

claims.title: Why it is expected never to halt
claims.text: If the parities of n behave like coin flips, the counter is a random walk with steps +2 and −1 (drift +1/2), which falls from m to −2 with chance φ−(m+2), φ the golden ratio: about 10−11 from the counter's value after 100 rounds.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known; a proof either way needs control of the parity sequence of an Antihydra-like orbit. A cryptid, probviously non-halting.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, and the reason is the same as for Antihydra: the machine multiplies a number by about 3/2 each round and keeps score of its parities. Even values push a counter up by two, odd values pull it down by one; it stops only if the counter ever falls below zero. Lean proves that this is exactly what the machine does.

facts.text: Halting reduced to an Antihydra-like map, proved in Lean.
The counter after 10<sup>5</sup> rounds; never below 1.
Chance it ever falls below zero, by a random-walk model.

sections.heading: A number and a counter
html: Every round starts with the head in state A at the left end of the tape, which reads

R n m  =  A> 0 11 (01)^n 0 11 (01)^m      (the number n, then the counter m)
Z k    =  A> 0 11 (01)^k                  (the counter used up)

In a round the head sweeps between the left end and the first 11. Each sweep takes two copies of 01 from the right of the 11 and writes three on its left, so the 11 walks through the number and the number grows by a factor 3/2. What is left over at the end, nothing or one copy, is the parity of n, and it decides what happens to the counter.
A round costs about n² steps, and n grows geometrically: the left part of the tape (the number) grows like the square root of the step count, the counter on the right like its logarithm.

sections.heading: Three halves, and a score of parities
html:
startn evenn odd, m ≥ 1n odd, m = 0
R n mR (3n/2+2) (m+2)R ((3n+7)/2) (m−1)Z ((3n+9)/2)

Z k goes to R ((3k+1)/2) 1 for odd k and halts for even k (the head runs off the right end in state F, which has no rule for a blank). Reading Z k as R (k−1) (−1), the machine halts exactly when an odd number meets the counter at −1. From blank tape it reaches Z 1 after 10 steps:

sections.heading: Only if the odd values win
html: The counter goes up by 2 for each even n and down by 1 for each odd one; the machine halts iff it ever falls below zero. Its lowest values were 1, at rounds 1 and 4; after 105 rounds it is 50,008 (49,997 odd rounds, 50,003 even ones).

If the parities behave like fair coin flips, the counter drifts upward by one half a round, and the chance of ever coming back down from m is φ−(m+2) with φ the golden ratio: about 10−11 already from round 100. This is Antihydra's situation: everyone expects it to run forever, and nobody can prove that the parities of a 3/2-map are balanced enough.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.052).
After 109 steps the tape spans 62,542 cells (44,518 left of the start, 45 right), with a density of 1s of 0.71.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Antihydra variant: halts iff a counter driven by the parities of n ↦ ~3n/2 (+2 even, −1 odd) falls below zero; reduction proved in Lean, counter at 50,008 after 10<sup>5</sup> rounds.
